title: electronica 2026 Breaks Records as Electronics Industry Gathers in Munich
html:
Four days, thousands of innovations, and countless conversations. electronica 2026 closed its doors in Munich on November 13 after welcoming more than 86,000 visitors and 3,512 exhibitors, setting new records for the international electronics trade fair.

But beyond the numbers, the event was about the people behind the technology. Engineers, researchers, startups, and industry leaders filled the exhibition halls, sharing ideas, discussing challenges, and exploring what comes next for electronics.

For eeNews Europe readers, electronica 2026 provided a valuable look at the technologies shaping the industry, from artificial intelligence and semiconductor manufacturing to energy-efficient electronics. It was also an opportunity to meet the people developing these solutions and hear their perspectives firsthand.

Record Attendance and a Truly International Event

The scale of electronica 2026 reflected the industry’s international reach. Exhibitors came from 60 countries and regions, with 74% traveling from outside Germany. Visitors represented 107 countries and regions, and 54% came from abroad.

Artificial intelligence dominated many discussions, with applications ranging from smart sensors and connected systems to automated manufacturing.

Energy efficiency, cybersecurity, and edge computing were also prominent. The new edge lab LIVE! area attracted visitors interested in seeing practical applications of edge computing through live demonstrations and workshops.

Celebrating Ten Years of electronica Fast Forward

Startups also had an important place at this year’s event, particularly through the tenth-anniversary edition of electronica Fast Forward, a startup program organized in cooperation with Elektor.

The program gave emerging electronics companies an opportunity to present their technologies, connect with potential partners, and exchange ideas with experienced industry professionals.

Among the participating startups were BTRY, developing ultra-thin batteries; Synthara, working on in-memory computing; DeepGate, focusing on efficient AI at the edge; HCP Sense, developing bearing-monitoring technology; and YPlasma, exploring ultra-thin plasma cooling.

Each company approached a different technical challenge, offering visitors a chance to discover new ideas and speak directly with the people developing them.

Europe’s Semiconductor Industry Takes Center Stage

Running alongside electronica, SEMICON Europa brought semiconductor manufacturing into focus, celebrating ten years of cooperation with Messe München.

The event featured an expanded exhibition area, the new NextSEMI ARENA, and a hackathon.

Europe’s technological competitiveness was another major topic. Representatives from Infineon, NXP, and STMicroelectronics discussed the region’s position in the global semiconductor market, alongside opportunities in Physical AI and Edge AI.

There were also encouraging economic indicators. According to the German Electro and Digital Industry Association (ZVEI), new orders increased by almost 13% between January and September 2026.

However, ZVEI President Daniel Hager stressed that better conditions for investment remain essential if Europe is to benefit from these opportunities.

Looking Ahead to electronica 2028

Beyond product demonstrations and technical presentations, electronica once again showed the value of meeting face to face.

Whether discussing a new semiconductor technology, discovering an unfamiliar startup, or reconnecting with industry colleagues, the four days offered opportunities that extend well beyond the exhibition halls.

The next electronica will take place in Munich from November 14 to 17, 2028.
